name: Dashboarding Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on dashboarding so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on dashboarding so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When dashboarding guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Keep dashboarding changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Check that dashboarding terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to dashboarding (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Prefer the simplest dashboarding approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. When multiple dashboarding strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. State assumptions about dashboarding explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting dashboarding assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated dashboarding concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of dashboarding correctness.
- Do not silently drop dashboarding edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic dashboarding advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for dashboarding, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
